name: Architecture Fit
checks: Every new/changed data table is documented in architecture docs (table, purpose, fields, constraints, indexes, sensitive tag)
Every new/changed workflow has a Workflow ID and covers: trigger, input validation, auth check, external calls, state changes, success response, failure response, idempotency strategy
Truth boundaries are explicit — which store is authority vs derived/projection
Storage areas define: access mode (public/private/signed), lifecycle (temp/permanent), authority vs derived
New components map to the role taxonomy (entrypoint/orchestrator/worker/adapter/scheduler/handler/DAL) with clear responsibility
Traceability matrix updated: Workflow ID -> file path -> DB table -> storage path -> external service
Non-goals have not been violated (features explicitly excluded have not been sneaked in)
ADR table reflects any new design decisions made during implementation
Document role & authority labels are correct (authority/companion/reference)
Repo/code structure mapping reflects any new directories or moved files
Human surfaces vs truth clarity check — UI/surface layers are clearly distinguished from truth-owning layers; no surface is silently treated as authority
Current vs Target topology clarity check — current-state architecture and target-state architecture are clearly separated; no target topology masquerading as current
Documentation maintenance is mandatory — architecture docs MUST be updated when schema, workflow, truth-boundary, integration, or deployment topology changes; stale docs are a conformance failure
Change Trigger Rules defined and followed — doc must be updated when: schema changes, workflow changes, truth-boundary changes, integration changes, deployment topology changes

checks.check: Reference versus clone: what may be consulted, what may be copied, and what may only be learned from.
Take every row in `.v4/facts.<repo>.json` under `auth_decision`, open the code at its `seen_at`, and say whether that symbol can refuse. Report the ones that carry an auth word and decide nothing.
checks.why_not_a_checker: A symbol named `has_brand_context` that reads a dict key and never raises is syntactically indistinguishable from one that gates. The table is the vocabulary 7 of 28 detectors read, so a row that decides nothing turns `route-auth` green for every handler that reaches it. Deciding whether a name is a decision is domain knowledge, not syntax.

checks.check: Read the facts table against how this repo actually decides who may do what. Name one way permission is granted or refused here that has no row.
checks.why_not_a_checker: `v4 install` proposes rows by matching a dotted call against 30 verbs. Measured on the reference adopter: it proposed 2 of 16 `auth_decision` rows; the other 14 are enum members (`Permission.DENY`), module constants (`TOOL_PERMISSIONS`) and regexes. Re-running the scan today produces 540 candidates of which almost all are dict lookups. There is no scan that finds what is missing -- only a reader.

anti_patterns: Target doc pretending to be current-state doc
No truth boundaries defined (who is authority, who is projection)
Donor/legacy repo implicitly treated as authority for new system
Runtime helpers silently becoming truth by convenience
Architecture doc updated without traceability (workflows cannot be traced to code)
Unresolved alternatives presented as active choices (evaluating tech listed as decided)
No non-goals defined — architecture doc lacks explicit exclusions, making scope creep undetectable
No phaseability — architecture treats everything as one monolithic delivery with no incremental path
No companion topology — architecture doc exists alone without companion docs (flowcharts, runtime profile) to triangulate correctness
Giant action-capability inventory without consolidation — doc lists every possible action/capability without grouping or prioritizing, obscuring actual architecture
No change trigger rules — doc has no explicit rules for when it must be updated, leading to silent drift
Template-filled but weak reasoning — architecture doc has all required sections filled in but reasoning is shallow/copy-pasted, not reflecting actual design decisions
Platform handbook style (tool-centric, not boundary-centric) — doc organized around tools/frameworks instead of responsibility boundaries and truth ownership

Direct DB mutation in feature delivery code — state-changing feature code bypasses canonical orchestration path (e.g. `db.execute("UPDATE ...")` in handler/entry layer instead of `service.update_state()`); violates ARCHITECTURE_GUIDELINES §7.5A; skips audit log / approval / cache invalidation / notification

Read-back from projection in Step 5 runtime proof — runtime proof `read-back` queries cache / UI / app log / response body instead of truth owner (DB truth table / audit log / external sandbox API); violates ARCHITECTURE_GUIDELINES §7.5B; projection may be stale or agent-controlled
